key_insight: No reconstruction method wins across all flow regimes: classical estimators remain competitive, while learned models gain an advantage as sensing becomes sparse or less informative.
engineering_relevance: Choose sparse-sensor reconstruction methods by flow regime, observed variables, uncertainty needs and computational budget rather than assuming learned models are always superior.
method: Compare 10 learned and 5 classical methods across cylinder wakes, 2D Kolmogorov turbulence and 3D isotropic turbulence.
Use leakage-controlled splits and shared sensor draws for consistent comparisons.
Evaluate per-channel error, ensemble spread, calibration, spectra and computational cost.
evidence_signal: Classical methods lead on cylinder wakes, inverse-distance weighting matches leading learned methods on observed 3D channels, and Kolmogorov rankings differ between pointwise error and probabilistic scoring.
watch_item: Generative ensembles remain underdispersed, and improving ensemble quality with larger sampler budgets increases computational cost.
paper_title: FlowReconBench: Accuracy, calibration and cost of learned and classical flow reconstruction from sparse sensors
